result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description states that two or more activities are performed independently, by different teams or systems, and a later step can proceed only after all of them have finished: Model a parallel gateway that forks the flow before the independent activities and a parallel gateway that joins them before the first step that needs all of them, instead of a sequential chain or an exclusive gateway.

When the description names several activities that are carried out side by side, with no stated order among them, and a later step starts only after all of them are finished: Model a parallel split gateway before the group of activities, with one unconditional outgoing flow to each activity. Join the activities with a parallel join gateway, and connect one outgoing flow from that join to the later step. Do not add decision conditions to these branches, and do not chain the activities in sequence when the description does not order them.

When the description states that an activity is performed on selected items, and only afterwards does the process branch according to a choice that each item states about how the next step is carried out: Model the stated activity as its own task, placed after the preceding step and connected to it by a sequence flow. Place the decision gateway after that task, not directly after the preceding step, so that the stated activity appears in the model and the branches are driven by the condition each item states.

When the description states that one step is completed by one of several alternative actions, listed with 'or' or 'whether it is X, Y or Z', and the alternatives are not merged into one activity by the description: Model each alternative action as its own task placed after an exclusive gateway that splits the flow, and join the alternative tasks with an exclusive merge gateway before the next step. Do not model the alternatives as one task whose label lists all options.
